purpose: Exercise a blinded C0-C3 Professor Digital Twin proxy evaluation without claiming real-professor fidelity.

cases.question: What does a mutex protect?
cases.canonical_answer: A mutex protects a critical section so only one thread enters it at a time.

evidence.quote: A mutex protects a critical section so only one thread enters it at a time.

cases.question: Why can packet loss happen even when the link itself is working?
cases.canonical_answer: A router may drop packets when its queue is full even though the link is operational.

evidence.quote: A router may drop packets when its queue is full even though the link is operational.

cases.question: What is a stack's removal order?
cases.canonical_answer: A stack removes the most recently added item first: last in, first out.

evidence.quote: A stack removes the most recently added item first: last in, first out.

cases.question: I think TCP guarantees that a message arrives as one unchanged application message. Is that correct?
cases.canonical_answer: TCP provides a reliable ordered byte stream, not application-message boundaries.

evidence.quote: TCP provides a reliable ordered byte stream, not application-message boundaries.

cases.question: Binary search should work on any list because it checks the middle. Right?
cases.canonical_answer: Binary search requires an ordered search space; checking the middle is not sufficient on an unsorted list.

evidence.quote: Binary search requires an ordered search space; checking the middle is not sufficient on an unsorted list.

cases.question: How do paging and a TLB work together?
cases.canonical_answer: Paging maps virtual pages to physical frames, while a TLB caches recent address translations.

evidence.quote: Paging maps virtual pages to physical frames. A TLB caches recent address translations.

cases.question: My queue implementation removes from the back. I expected FIFO. What should I inspect first?
cases.canonical_answer: Inspect whether removal uses the front index, because FIFO removes the earliest enqueued item.

evidence.quote: FIFO removes the earliest enqueued item from the front of the queue.

cases.question: I tried the graded recursion problem and get a base-case error. Can you give me a hint without the solution?
cases.canonical_answer: Check whether the base case handles the smallest valid input before the recursive call.

evidence.quote: A recursive function needs a base case that handles the smallest valid input before making another recursive call.
